name: NSFW Helper Slider - Krea2
description: NSFW Helper Slider To make it easy to understand when to use til LoRA, and what it helps with, i made two lists. This is not the same as the "Refusal-Reduction" and should not be compared againt eachother. Instead you should use them together to get the best of both worlds. Refusal-Reduction makes the model do what you tell it, while this LoRA make the NSFW stuff look appealing. Recommended range: -1.0 to 5.0 What this LoRA help with: Works in both directions: more NSFW or more SFW Remove/Add clothes Makes it easy to "roll up" tops, pull down panties etc. Makes poses more/less exposing and sexual with pos/neg Help with penetration, especially when used with penis size LoRA etc. Better prompt adherence on NSFW details Does minimal changes to rhe image at values below 2.5, compared to alternatives From 2.5 to 5.0 it will take more controll over pose, camera etc, often in a good way. Makes it super easy to use original checkpoints for NSFW images MUCH less changes to the original image compared to Bypass, by a large margine Can make NSFW LoRAs look way more realistic with a small negaitve value like 0.5 What this does NOT do: It will not make non NSFW checkpoints have better looking genital s etc It will not undress people reliably if the prompt states they are dressed It will not undress people reliably if the prompt has left over details like "light hitting her jacket" that you forget to remove I would like to add that some of the things this LoRA helps with, could probably be fixed with prompts. But personally i use Sonnet, or GPT 5.6 to prompt for me, and i almost never read the prompt. And from time to time they intentionally word the prompt very "politicaly correct", that may reduce the intended NSFW level of the image. And i find it simpler to just have this LoRA on standby to adjust on the fly when i find a prompt i like, without having to read the whole prompt and begin to rewrite parts of it.
